title: How to Compliment a Guy: 8 Quick Tips With Real Examples
h1: How to Compliment a Guy: 8 Quick Tips (With Examples You Can Use Today)
description: Learn how to compliment a guy in a way that feels genuine. 8 quick tips with real examples for praising his effort, character, style, mind and more.
excerpt: Eight practical ways to compliment a guy sincerely, from his effort and character to his style and good decisions, with examples for each.
intro:
Plenty of men go weeks, even months, without hearing a sincere compliment. Many will tell you they still remember a nice thing someone said to them years ago. That says a lot about how rare and how meaningful genuine praise can be.

If you want to know how to compliment a guy, whether he's your partner, your crush or a friend, the secret isn't flowery language. It's being specific and honest. Below are eight quick tips, each with examples you can adapt, plus a few notes on timing and delivery so your words land the way you mean them.
body:
Why Specific Compliments Work Best

"You're great" is nice. "I loved how patient you were with your nephew today" is unforgettable. Specific compliments prove you were paying attention, and that's what makes them feel real. They also tell him what you value, which is useful information in any relationship.

A simple formula: what you noticed + why it mattered to you. "You fixed my bike without me even asking. It made my whole week easier." Keep that pattern in mind as you read the tips below.

1. Compliment His Effort, Not Just the Result

Results aren't always in someone's control, but effort is. Praising effort tells him you see the work behind the scenes, not just the trophy at the end.

  • "You've been putting in so many hours on that project. I really admire how committed you are."
  • "I can tell you practiced. That speech was so smooth."
  • "Even though the game didn't go your way, you never stopped hustling."

These work especially well after a setback, when he may be feeling like his effort didn't count.

2. Show That You Believe in Him

Few things are more motivating than knowing someone is in your corner. A compliment that expresses confidence in him can carry him through a stressful week.

  • "You're going to do great in that interview. You know your stuff."
  • "If anyone can figure this out, it's you."
  • "I've seen how you handle pressure. You've got this."
Tip: Belief compliments are most powerful right before something hard: an exam, a job interview, a tough conversation. A quick text that morning can mean more than a long speech later.

3. Praise His Character

Looks change and achievements fade, but character is who he is. Compliments about his values tend to stick with him the longest.

  • "I love how kind you are to people who can't do anything for you."
  • "You're one of the most honest people I know."
  • "The way you show up for your friends says so much about you."
  • "You make people feel comfortable. That's a real gift."

4. Compliment His Appearance (Thoughtfully)

Yes, guys like hearing they look good too, and many rarely hear it. The trick is to be specific and to focus on things he chose, like his style, his haircut or how he carries himself.

  • "That color looks really good on you."
  • "Your new haircut suits you."
  • "You have a great smile. It lights up your whole face."
  • "You clean up nicely. I like this look on you."

If you're just getting to know him, keep appearance compliments light and friendly. Comments about his body are best saved for when you're in a relationship and you both know they're welcome.

5. Appreciate His Intelligence and Wisdom

Recognizing how he thinks shows you respect his mind, not just his company.

  • "I never thought about it that way. That's a really smart point."
  • "You explain things so clearly."
  • "I always learn something when we talk."
  • "Your advice last week really helped me. Thank you."

Asking for his opinion on something you care about is a compliment in itself. It tells him you value his perspective.

6. Show Respect for What He Does

Respect is something many men say they want to feel from their partners and friends. You can express it by noticing his competence and his role in your life.

  • "I really respect how you handled that situation."
  • "You're so good with your hands. I'm impressed every time."
  • "I love watching you do what you're passionate about."
  • "I trust your judgment."

If you want to understand this need more deeply, our post on what men want in a relationship explores it further.

7. Compliment His Decisions

Many people second-guess themselves after a big choice. Backing up a decision he made, when you genuinely agree with it, can be a huge relief.

  • "Choosing that restaurant was a great call."
  • "I think taking that job was really brave."
  • "You handled that conversation with your brother really well."

Only offer this kind of praise when you mean it. Empty agreement doesn't help anyone, and he'll likely sense it.

8. Acknowledge His Feelings

Plenty of men grow up hearing that emotions are something to hide. Telling him you appreciate his openness can make it feel safer for him to share.

  • "Thank you for telling me how you felt. It means a lot that you trust me."
  • "I love how much you care about the people around you."
  • "It's really attractive that you're so in touch with what you feel."

This is one of the most underrated compliments you can give, and it builds real emotional closeness over time.

How to Deliver a Compliment So It Lands

  • Mean it. If you don't believe it, don't say it. Sincerity matters more than wording.
  • Keep it short. One or two sentences is plenty. Overdoing it can make him uncomfortable.
  • Don't attach a request. A compliment followed by "So can you..." feels like a setup.
  • Mix the medium. Say it in person, text it, or leave a note in his bag. Written compliments get reread.
  • Let him react however he reacts. Many guys deflect with a joke because they aren't used to praise. That doesn't mean it didn't matter.

Compliments to skip

Some compliments land awkwardly even when they're meant kindly. A few to avoid:

  • Backhanded praise. "You actually look good today" or "That was smarter than I expected" stings more than it flatters.
  • Comparisons. "You're so much better than my ex" pulls someone else into the moment. Keep the focus on him.
  • Praise tied to stereotypes. "You're so manly for crying at that movie" mixes a compliment with a judgment. Just say you love how open he is.
  • Constant, automatic compliments. If every sentence includes praise, it starts to sound like filler. A few meaningful ones beat a stream of generic ones.

Match the compliment to the relationship

How you compliment a guy depends a lot on who he is to you.

  • A new crush: keep it light and specific. "You have the best laugh" or "You always have great music recommendations" shows interest without too much pressure.
  • A boyfriend or husband: go deeper. Compliment the way he parents, the way he supports you, or how he's grown over the years you've been together.
  • A friend or coworker: focus on skills and character. "You handled that meeting really well" or "You're always the one who checks in on everyone" is warm without being romantic.

When in doubt, ask yourself whether you'd be comfortable if someone else overheard the compliment. If the answer is yes, it's probably a good fit for the relationship.

If you're complimenting a crush, pair this with our tips on how to start a conversation with a guy over text and how to get a guy to like you. Want the other side? See how to compliment a girl.

In the end, learning how to compliment a guy is really about noticing him: his effort, his choices, his kindness and the little things he does without being asked. Say what you see, say why it matters to you, and keep it honest. Do that regularly and you'll strengthen whatever connection you share, whether it's a friendship, a new crush or a long-term relationship.
takeaways: Specific compliments feel more genuine than general ones.
Praise his effort, character and decisions, not only his looks.
Acknowledging his feelings builds emotional closeness.
Keep compliments short, sincere and free of strings attached.

faq.q: What is the best compliment for a guy?
faq.a: The best compliment is a specific, sincere one about something he values in himself, such as his kindness, his humor, his effort or a decision he made. For example: 'I really admire how you stayed calm when everything went wrong today.' Compliments about character tend to stick with men longer than comments about looks.

faq.q: How do I compliment a guy without being awkward?
faq.a: Keep it short, casual and specific, then move the conversation along. A quick 'That shirt looks really good on you' or 'You're really funny' works well in the flow of normal conversation. Avoid long speeches and don't wait for a big reaction. Many guys deflect compliments with a joke, which is normal.

faq.q: How do you compliment a guy over text?
faq.a: Text compliments work well because he can reread them. Mention something specific from your last conversation or something he shared, like 'I keep thinking about that story you told me, you're such a good storyteller.' Keep the tone natural and don't overload one message with too many compliments at once.

faq.q: Do guys like being complimented on their looks?
faq.a: Many do, especially since men often receive fewer appearance compliments than women. Focus on things he chose, like his style, haircut or smile. When you're just getting to know someone, keep it light and friendly. More personal compliments about his body are best for established relationships where you both know they're welcome.
